sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Palm Beach County?
sections.html:
The Palm Beach County Constitutional Tax Collector mails the bills and takes payment, while the Property Appraiser sets the value and decides exemptions. Two offices, two jobs, and a mix-up between them is the most common reason an owner calls the wrong number.

The tax collector's page says its office mails more than 600,000 property tax bills by November 1 each year, and that bills go to the address the Property Appraiser has on file. If you moved or sold, fix the address with the appraiser, not the collector. The appraiser's exemption desk is at 561.355.2866, and the collector's delinquent-tax line printed on the bill page is (561) 355-2264.

The clerk and comptroller is the third office you will meet. It runs the Value Adjustment Board that hears appeals, and it conducts tax deed sales if a certificate ever reaches that stage.

  • Palm Beach County Property Appraiser: values, exemptions, caps, the TRIM notice.
  • Palm Beach County Tax Collector: bills, payment, installment plan, deferral, certificates.
  • Clerk and Comptroller: Value Adjustment Board petitions and tax deed sales.

sections.h2: What does Palm Beach County look like for a home seller?
sections.html:
It is a large, mostly built-out coastal county, and the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page counts 1,575,726 residents as of July 1, 2025 across 1,964.30 square miles of land. That works out to 759.7 people per square mile in 2020, with a lot of the density packed along the Atlantic side.

The same page gives a 2020 to 2024 median value of owner-occupied homes of $447,300 and an owner-occupied rate of 70.1 percent. Median household income was $83,581 in 2024 dollars. People 65 and older make up 26.1 percent of residents, which matters here because senior and veteran exemptions are a real part of many tax bills.

The property appraiser's municipality list shows how many separate taxing authorities exist. Its codes run from 00 for unincorporated areas through towns and cities such as Atlantis, Belle Glade, Boca Raton, Boynton Beach, Delray Beach, Jupiter, Lake Worth Beach, Palm Beach, Pahokee, Tequesta, Wellington, West Palm Beach and Westlake. The first two digits of a 17-digit parcel control number carry that code, so the number on your bill tells you which city levies on your lot.

sections.h2: When are Palm Beach County property taxes due, and what discounts apply?
sections.html:
Bills are payable from November 1 through March 31, and an early payment discount shrinks each month. The tax collector prints the schedule as 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February, with the gross amount due in March.

April 1 is the delinquency date. After that the bill carries penalties and interest, it cannot be paid online, and the collector says payment must arrive by the last working day of the month because a postmark no longer counts. A date that lands on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day under Florida law.

The county's installment plan lets you prepay in pieces. The tax collector's 2026 calendar lists an application deadline of April 30, a first payment that earns a discount due June 30, a hard cutoff of July 31 for the first payment, a second payment September 30 and a third December 31. Enrollment for the following year opens November 1. Check the tax collector's calendar for the year you are in before relying on those days.

sections.h2: How do the homestead exemption and the assessment caps work in Palm Beach County?
sections.html:
A homestead exemption lowers the taxable value of your primary home, and a cap limits how fast its assessed value can climb. The county appraiser says you must be a permanent Florida resident holding title and living in the home as of January 1, and you must file by March 1 or you waive the exemption for that year.

The appraiser describes a $25,000 exemption on the first $50,000 of assessed value that applies to every tax, school taxes included. State rules add a second layer of up to $25,000 on value above $50,000 for non-school taxes. Filing is done online, in person at a service center, or by mailed form, and once approved the exemption renews itself each year. A receipt card is mailed on the last business day of December.

The Save Our Homes cap holds a homestead's yearly assessment increase to the lower of 3 percent or the inflation figure. The state's chart shows a 2026 cap of 2.7 percent. Non-homestead property, such as a rental or second home, has a 10 percent cap on every taxing authority except the school board, and the appraiser notes that the cap falls away the year after a sale.

  • Report any change in ownership, marriage, divorce, death or use of the home to the appraiser at 561.355.2866 or MyExemption@pbcpao.gov.
  • An exemption does not move to a new house on its own. A new application is required, and portability can carry part of your capped savings over if you start a new homestead within three years.
  • Renting out the home, or ceasing to live in it, ends the homestead.

sections.h2: What happens to the property tax when I sell a house in Palm Beach County?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax follows the property, not the seller, so it gets settled at closing. The title company reads the open bill, pays it from the seller's proceeds, and the buyer receives a clean title for that parcel.

Ask the title company how it splits the current year's bill between you and the buyer, since the bill is issued in November and closings happen all year.

The deed itself carries the state documentary stamp tax. Florida's statute sets it at 70 cents on each $100 of consideration for deeds in every county except Miami-Dade, and all parties to the document are liable, whichever one agrees to pay. The clerk collects it when the deed is recorded. The clerk's recording charge starts at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus trust fund and technology charges.

For the buyer, the sale resets the assessed value to market value the next January 1. The seller's capped homestead savings do not transfer to the buyer, which is why the neighbor's bill can look so different from the new owner's.

sections.h2: What if I am behind on Palm Beach County property taxes?
sections.html:
Missing the March 31 deadline starts a chain that ends, after two years, with a possible tax deed sale. It moves in clear steps, and you can stop it by paying at any point before the sale.

The tax collector says it is required to hold an annual tax certificate sale, no earlier than 60 days after delinquency or June 1, whichever is later. A certificate is a first lien that an investor buys by paying your tax. To redeem one, you pay the delinquent tax, accrued interest, advertising costs and an added $6.25 collection fee. Certificates the investors skip become county held and accrue interest at 18 percent a year, printed as 1.5 percent a month.

If two years pass from the delinquency date without payment, the certificate holder can file a tax deed application, and the clerk's office runs the sale. You can still redeem any time before the sale happens. Homestead owners who are 65 or older, or have lower income, may also ask the collector's office about the deferral program, which has its own state rules and a March 31 filing date in state materials.

  • Delinquent payments cannot be made online; use the collector's listed delivery options.
  • Call (561) 355-2264 if the bill shows a delinquent notice.
  • An owner behind on tax can still sell. The title company pays the lien from proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Palm Beach County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with an informal call to the Property Appraiser, then file a petition with the Value Adjustment Board if that does not settle it. The appraiser's FAQ encourages the call first, with records searchable on its site or by phone at 561.355.3230.

The calendar the appraiser publishes says market value appeals and denied portability applications are due to the board in mid-September, while appeals of denied exemptions are due by July 31 or 30 days after the denial notice is mailed. The state tax-payer page separately gives 25 days from the Notice of Proposed Taxes for a value petition. Read the dates on your own notice, since the notice controls.

The Value Adjustment Board is run by the clerk and comptroller, independent of the appraiser. Ask the Palm Beach clerk for the current filing fee before you file.

faqs.q: Who do I pay if I owe Palm Beach County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Palm Beach County Tax Collector. The office mails bills by November 1, takes payment through its online portal and service centers, and handles delinquent accounts at (561) 355-2264. The Property Appraiser sets value but does not collect.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying early in Palm Beach County?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax collector prints 4 percent for November, 3 percent for December, 2 percent for January and 1 percent for February, with no discount in March. April 1 starts delinquency, with penalties and interest.

faqs.q: Do I lose my homestead exemption if I sell my Palm Beach County home?
faqs.a: Yes, the exemption ends with the sale and does not transfer to the buyer. Start a new homestead by March 1 of the year you want it, and ask the appraiser at 561.355.2866 about portability if you buy another Florida home within three years.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Palm Beach County house that has unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid tax is a lien on the parcel, and the title company pays it from the seller's proceeds at closing. If a tax certificate has already been sold, the redemption amount includes interest, advertising costs and a $6.25 collection fee.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Palm Beach County?
faqs.a: Record it with the clerk and comptroller, who keeps the official records. Florida's statute sets the base recording charge at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 per added page, plus other statutory charges, and the deed also needs the 70 cents per $100 documentary stamp tax.
